 SCCH.13 3 MVC.3638/2022  J U D G M E N T
This petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989 is filed seeking compensation for the death of Sri Prasanth Raja S/o Raja Venu in a road traffic accident.
Due to the impact, Prasanth Raja and other inmates sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was taken to Govt. hospital, Chinthamani, wherein the duty doctors examined and declared dead and thereafter postmortem was conducted and handed over the dead body to the Petitioners.
3. It is stated that the accident and death was due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The deceased was aged about 29 years, running hotel of his own at Tamilnadu and was earning .30,000/ p.m.

The Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioner No.2 is the daughter, Petitioner No.3 & 4 are the parents of deceased and they were depending upon the income of deceased and due to untimely death of Prasanth Raja, they have suffered mental shock and agony and lost their bread earner of the family.

As the Petitioners have spent .1,00,000/ for funeral and other expenses also,
it is requested to award .75,00,000/ compensation with interest from the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the insured and insurer of the offending vehicle.
P.Lavanya vs Pidikondala Prthvi on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198107925/
2 4. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.2 has appeared before the court through its counsel and filed its objection.
The Respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court and he was placed exparte.

5. The 2nd Respondent in its objection statement admitted the issuance of policy in favour of offending vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident and its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It has contended that the owner of the offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further it has contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid driving license and it has no valid FC and permit at the time of accident.
It has denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and contended that compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant and prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioners prove that the death of Prashanth Raja @ Prashanth S/o Raja Venu @ Raja Renu @ Raja was only due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Innova Car vehicle bearing No.AP39GY 1344 on 12052022 about 7.30 p.m. at Signahahalli village, Chinthamani Taluk, Chikkaballapura District?

2. What compensation Petitioners are entitled?
3. What order ?

7. In support of their claim, 1st Petitioner is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.14.
8.
The Respondent No.2 has not chosen to adduce any oral and documentary evidence.
9. I heard the counsel on both sides and have perused the material on record.

10. By considering the evidence and materials available on record and after hearing the arguments my findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 11. ISSUE NO.1: Petitioners say that on 12052022 about 730 p.m. Prasanth Raja and others were proceeding in a Innova Car bearing No.AP39GY1344 from Ramasamudram town via Srinivasapura, at Singanahalli village, Chintamani Taluk, Chikkaballapura District, its driver drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, lost control and dashed against right portion of Swift car bearing No.KA02MD1828 and then dashed a tractor from behind.

Due to the impact, Prasanth P.Lavanya vs Pidikondala Prthvi on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198107925/
3
Raja and other inmates sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was taken to Govt. hospital,
Chinthamani, wherein the duty doctors examined and declared him dead.
Petitioners say that it was the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

They relied on the police records and submitted that the police have filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle and it is requested to award compensation from the owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle.

12. In support of their version Petitioners have produced FIR, Complaint, spot mahazar, spot sketch,
IMV report, Inquest report, PM report and Charge sheet at Ex.P1 to 8.
13.
To prove the negligence on the part driver of the offending vehicle, 1st Petitioner examined herself as PW1 and she relied on the police records.
Respondentinsurance company has denied petition averments and generally denied all the allegations made against the driver of the offending vehicle and denied his rash and negligent driving.
PW1 is not an eyewitness and no suggestion could be made to her with regard to negligence.
The Respondent insurance company has not placed any materials to disprove the negligence of driver of the offending vehicle.
14. Police have filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
All the materials clearly indicate that the accident was due to the negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
Based on the entire records, I hold that the driver of offending vehicle was negligent in causing the accident due to which the Prasanth Raja died due to injuries sustained in the RTA.
Hence, this Issue is answered in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.2:
Petitioners states that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Prasanth Raja.
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioner No.2 is the daughter and Petitioner No.3 and 4 are the parents of the deceased.

They have produced the Aadhaar card of deceased at Ex.P.9, the PAN card and Aadhaar cards of Petitioner No.1, birth certificate of Petitioner No.2, Aadhaar card of Petitioner No.3 and 4 are produced at Ex.P.10 to 14, which clearly indicates that and the husband of first Petitioner.
It is clear that the Petitioner No.2 is the daughter of the deceased Prasanth Raja.
Hence, I hold that the Petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased and they are entitled for compensation as dependents.
16. It is stated that the deceased was 29 years old and was running a hotel in the name and style of Raja Hotel at Tamil Nadu and earning .30,000/ p.m. and was the sole earning member of the family.
In order to show the avocation and income of the deceased Petitioners have not produced any supportive documents.
Considering the age of the deceased and the date of accident and in the absence of proof of income, notional income of .15,500/ per month is taken.
17. According to the ExP9 Aadhar card, the year of the birth of deceased is mentioned as 1994.
As per this document his age was 28 years as on the date of accident and same is considered as age of the deceased and proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 17.
As the age of the deceased is below 40 years, 40% future prospects is to be added as per Pranay Sethi case.

Then the monthly income would be .15,500+6,200=.21,700/.As there are 4 dependents, as per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 1/4th of the income to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses and then the annual P.Lavanya vs Pidikondala Prthvi on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198107925/
4 income would come around .16,275x12 = .1,95,300/ and by applying 17 multiplier, the loss of dependency would be .33,20,100/.

sentences.text: 18. CONSORTIUM:

By following the guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others.1, this Tribunal deems it proper to hold that the Petitioners are entitled .40,000/ each under the head of consortium as Petitioner No.1 has lost her 1 (2018) 18 SCC 130 husband, Petitioner No.2 has lost her father and Petitioner No.3 and 4 have lost their son.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others.1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 19. Loss to estate:
It appears that the Petitioner No.1 has lost her husband at her younger age and the daughter has lost their father and parents have lost their son.
Hence, .20,000/ towards loss to estate.
20. Funeral Expenses:
Petitioners have claimed that they have spent .1,00,000/ towards transportation of dead body, funeral & obsequies ceremony expenses.
By considering the facts and circumstances it would be proper to award .15,000/ for the funeral and other incidental expenses.
21. In all, the amount of compensation awarded by this Tribunal to the Petitioner under various headings is as follows :
Sl . No Nature of Compensation Amount 1. Loss of dependency .

2. Loss of consortium . 1,60,000/
3. Loss to estate . 20,000/
4. Transportation of . 15,000/ dead body, Funeral & obsequies Expenses Total .
35,15,100/
22.
Liability:
The Petitioners have lead cogent evidence and have proved that the accident was occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of offending vehicle.
The policy was in force as on the date of accident.

Hence, Respondents being owner and insurer of offending vehicle shall pay compensation to the Petitioners with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., With these observations, I have answered Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
23. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.
Petitioners are awarded compensation of .35,15,100/ together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the realization.
P.Lavanya vs Pidikondala Prthvi on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198107925/
5
Respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation amount within three months from the date of this Order.

After deposit of amount, 60% of the amount is apportioned to 1st Petitioner and 20%
to the Petitioner No.2 and 10% each to Petitioner No.3 and 4.

Out of the said apportioned amount in respect of Petitioner No.1, 25% of the amount shall be kept in FD in her name in any nationalized or scheduled bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and balance 75% amount shall be disbursed to her through E payment on proper identification.
The entire apportioned amount in respect of Petitioner No.2 shall be kept in FD in any nationalized bank of Petitioner No.1's choice till she attains the age of majority.
Petitioner No.1 is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest on the FD.
The entire apportioned amount shall be disbursed to them through Epayment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at  .1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer, corrected, signed and pronounced by me in open court dated this the 18th day of January 2023).
